changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail store-operations buyers (COO, head of store ops): "One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket, one team accountable." In store-ops conversations, say "the tills" instead of "point of sale" or "in-person payments", and drop "unified commerce".
changes.why: The head of store ops dismissed M3 as "a diagram", while the customer described what she wanted in sharper operator words: "one system for the tills and the website" and "one customer, one basket"; she never said "unified commerce" or "point of sale".

changes.change: Proof point for retail operations audiences: "Watch an online order get returned at a store till, live, refunded to the original payment and on the same customer record." Show it step by step in the demo; do not describe it. Confirm the flow is demoable today before using this line.
changes.why: The evaluation started because stores could not see online orders at return time, and the store-ops lead asked to see a till return live; we described it and never showed it.

changes.change: For retailers planning a store rollout: "One team answerable for your store rollout: a named rollout lead and a plan with dates, who installs, and what happens to your old tills. No two vendors pointing at each other." Use this only where we can name the rollout lead and own install accountability; never answer "who shows up" with "a partner".
changes.why: The customer's stated fear was "two vendors pointing at each other", she asked for a rollout plan covering dates, installers and the old tills, and our "we'd bring in a partner" answer ended the store-ops lead's questions.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail decision-makers: "Talk to a retailer who runs our tills and website. We'll set up the call this week." Offer a live reference call, not a case study. Use this only once a standby list of omnichannel retail references is in place.
changes.why: The decider asked "can I talk to them?" and we could not set up a call in time, while the competitor reportedly named retailers she knew.
